newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian police arrest four after cinema fire.
newsitem.headline: Indian police arrest four after cinema fire.

text.p: Indian police have arrested four managers of a cinema in the capital where 57 people died in a fire, and more people are expected to be detained, a senior official said on Saturday.

Deputy police commissioner Maxwell Perreira told Reuters that authorities have accused the four managers of the Uphaar Grand cinema of criminal negligence in the fire which broke out in the packed movie theatre on Friday.
"We have arrested four people from the cinema's management," Perreira told Reuters by telephone. "More arrests are likely."

He said police had registered cases against the four for criminal negligence causing grievous hurt, causing deaths due to criminal negligence and use of combustible materials. The four were to be arraigned in a Delhi court on Saturday.

Perreira said a small fire had broken out on Friday morning in the transformer which hours later exploded during the premiere of a Hindi movie. "We will have to see to what extent the transformer was repaired," the police official said.
Most of the victims were trapped in the balcony and suffocated when poisonous smoke engulfed the theatre, which was packed to its capacity of 1,050 seats, Perreira said.
